skills.name: focusa-agent-bootstrap
skills.description: Use when orienting a new or resumed agent with bounded Focusa identity, Agent Card, progressive tool discovery, preload, Workpoint, and Trajectory context.
skills.done: Agent has verified scope, current Workpoint/Trajectory orientation, and only the schemas needed for the next action.

skills.name: focusa-tool-discovery
skills.description: Use when selecting or composing Focusa capabilities through search, describe, graph, family bundles, strict schemas, and cross-harness bindings without prompt bloat.
non_triggers: exact tool and schema already loaded
skills.done: The narrowest valid capability and dependency sequence are selected under token budget.

skills.name: focusa-project-scope
skills.description: Use when project root, continuity, repository, deployment, alias, or cross-project authority may be ambiguous before trusting state or mutating files.
skills.done: project_root plus continuity_id authority is verified and target objects resolve in that scope.

skills.name: focusa-session-recovery
skills.description: Use for compaction, model switch, context overflow, fork, rollover, session transfer, lineage snapshots, and canonical continuation recovery.
skills.done: A canonical Workpoint packet supplies mission, action, evidence, blockers, and exact next action.

skills.name: focusa-browser-uiai
skills.description: Use for UIAI-first browser research/action, WebMCP capability intake, session/origin isolation, diagnostics, evidence, and Workpoint linkage.
non_triggers: generic web fallback before UIAI health
skills.done: Browser result is proven in the bound session/origin, diagnostics are ingested, evidence is linked, and unused sessions are closed.

skills.name: focusa-install-lifecycle
skills.description: Use for supported install, first Workpoint, repair/rerun, trusted OTA update, rollback, uninstall, and preserved-user-data verification.
skills.done: The requested lifecycle state passes end-to-end proof with rollback/preservation evidence.

skills.name: focusa-security-auth-licensing
skills.description: Use for permissions, mutation confirmation, bearer/device pairing, revocation, license activation, secrets, and operator approval boundaries.
skills.done: Least-privilege scope, explicit approval, revocation/recovery, and secret-safe evidence are verified.

skills.name: focusa-resource-performance
skills.description: Use for LowMem/resource pressure, Bloatgaurd budgets, token control, bounded traversal, latency, and hot/cold route performance.
skills.done: Work completes inside declared memory/token/latency budgets with bounded payloads.

skills.name: focusa-mission-canvas
skills.description: Use for Mission Canvas, Work Rail, CRIST interviews, generated UI, workspace artifacts, live refresh, and provider-neutral operation binding.
skills.done: Generated UI binds canonical operations and durable workspace evidence without semantic drift.

skills.name: focusa-release-proof
skills.description: Use when preparing a release gate, proof bundle, changelog, resolved-issue audit, local quality evidence, and operator-authorized CI/release execution.
skills.done: Every acceptance criterion, issue, changelog entry, platform boundary, and evidence ref is verified before authorized release action.

skills.name: focusa-temporal-authority
skills.description: Use when deadlines, freshness, temporal evidence, prior-valid fallback, forecast windows, or stale-state decisions affect authority.
skills.done: Decision cites current temporal evidence, freshness, confidence, and bounded forecast/recovery.

skills.name: focusa-spec-implementation
skills.description: Use when turning a Focusa specification into a call-stack design, Trajectory gap, Beads tasks, bounded implementation, and conformance evidence.
skills.done: Implementation matches the typed call stack, acceptance criteria, task closure, and linked proof.

skills.name: focusa-evidence-outcomes
skills.description: Use for evidence refs, receipts, prediction evaluation, proposal settlement, project-card outcomes, acceptance truth, and false-completion prevention.
skills.done: Canonical outcome status is backed by stable evidence/receipt refs and evaluated learning signals.
